# mulib-mesh-core

<!-- Generated by tools/joltfx_inventory.py; edit CONTRACTS or section-7 scope, then --write-docs. -->

**Area:** Geometry  
**Implementation:** C11 `static inline`; no implementation switch or external ABI export  
**Status:** bounded review candidate; **not safe On1x admitted**

## Purpose and limits

Caller-owned indexed triangle mesh and vector math.

Triangle-only initial model; integrate canonical cgeom/linalg types later.

Retain existing upstream functionality and platform providers; this header is not a replacement for a complete media/editor/rendering stack.

## Units, ownership and capacities

append_vertex/append_tri require unused capacity and preserve uint32 index representability. Vector arithmetic helpers are low-level finite-input primitives, not allocation/bounds-checked foreign imports.

Meshes borrow indexed triangle and double-precision vec3 storage. vertex_count/vertex_capacity count vertices; triangle_count/triangle_capacity count triangles, not indices or bytes. Triangle indices are uint32_t. Use consistent caller-defined length units and finite positions; helpers do not supply exact predicates or full CAD topology.

Capacities describe live backing storage supplied by the caller, not merely numeric metadata. Check return values before using outputs. A false result is not a universal no-mutation guarantee; low-level value helpers and bool miss/error results require the documented preconditions. Bound untrusted counts and work before calling.

## Current callable surface

Signatures extracted from this header; dependency types and complete checks are in [the source](../include/mulib-mesh-core.h). Helpers listed here are not automatically safe foreign imports.

```c
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_mesh_v(double x,double y,double z);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_mesh_add(mulib_mesh_vec3 a,mulib_mesh_vec3 b);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_mesh_sub(mulib_mesh_vec3 a,mulib_mesh_vec3 b);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_mesh_scale(mulib_mesh_vec3 a,double t);
static inline double mulib_mesh_dot(mulib_mesh_vec3 a,mulib_mesh_vec3 b);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_mesh_cross(mulib_mesh_vec3 a,mulib_mesh_vec3 b);
static inline double mulib_mesh_length(mulib_mesh_vec3 a);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_mesh_unit(mulib_mesh_vec3 a);
static inline bool mulib_mesh_finite(mulib_mesh_vec3 v);
static inline bool mulib_mesh_disjoint(const void *a,size_t an,const void *b,size_t bn);
static inline bool mulib_mesh_storage_valid(const mulib_mesh *m);
static inline bool mulib_mesh_valid(const mulib_mesh *m);
static inline bool mulib_mesh_append_vertex(mulib_mesh *m,mulib_mesh_vec3 v,uint32_t *id);
static inline bool mulib_mesh_append_tri(mulib_mesh *m,uint32_t a,uint32_t b,uint32_t c);
```

## Additional source contracts

- Scale first: normalization also handles finite subnormal/very large vectors.
- Byte-span checks use uintptr_t on the supported flat-address targets. They do not prove allocation provenance: callers still supply actual live objects.
- Capacities/counts are elements, not bytes. Buffers must not overlap. This bootstrap double representation is NOT ABI-compatible with float linalg.

## Validation and integration

The [shared CPU example](../examples/joltfx-pipeline.c) illustrates a small image/audio/timebase slice; it does **not** exercise every API in this header. The [integration oracles](../tests/joltfx-integration-test.c) and [parser boundary probes](../tests/joltfx-parser-boundary-test.c) are representative regressions, not exhaustive coverage.

```sh
python3 tools/check_joltfx.py
```

The runner checks the 193 original kernels plus the shared PCM helper, isolated and in aggregate C11 builds with GCC/Clang, including canonical-header composition, separate-TU wrappers, an expected missing-static-inline-export link failure, a no-`__int128` path, and ASan/UBSan regressions. It does not validate native GPU/codec/audio execution, real-world compatibility, C++ or On1x ownership/admission. Explicit foreign wrappers, independent safety review and platform integration are still required.
